proposal.one_liner: Fathom is a Google Analytics alternative that makes your analytics easy to understand and respects visitor privacy.
proposal.promise: That you get a Google Analytics-grade view of your traffic and conversions without using cookies, collecting personal data, or showing a cookie banner — privacy-first analytics that stays simple.

claims.text: Fathom's hero tagline positions it as cookieless analytics
claims.verbatim: Analytics without the cookies

claims.text: Fathom describes itself as a Google Analytics alternative that is easy to understand and privacy-respecting
claims.verbatim: Fathom is a Google Analytics alternative that makes your analytics easy to understand and respects visitor privacy.

claims.text: Offers a 7-day free trial
claims.verbatim: 7-day free trial

claims.text: Customers can cancel anytime
claims.verbatim: Cancel anytime

claims.text: The whole company is built around digital privacy
claims.verbatim: Our entire company is built on putting digital privacy first.

claims.text: As a Canadian company, Fathom says it is covered by Canada's EU adequacy decision for EU traffic
claims.verbatim: as a Canadian company, we're covered by Canada's EU adequacy decision.

claims.text: Fathom says it is GDPR, CCPA, ePrivacy and PECR compliant
claims.verbatim: Plus, we're GDPR, CCPA, ePrivacy, PECR (and more) compliant.

claims.text: Fathom claims other analytics tools miss real visitors due to blockers, cookies and sampling
claims.verbatim: Plenty of analytics tools miss real people because of blockers, cookies and sampling.

claims.text: The tracking script loads without slowing down the page
claims.verbatim: Our lightweight script loads without holding up your page.

claims.text: Not collecting personal data means no cookie notice is needed

claims.text: No cookies means no consent banner is required
claims.verbatim: Fathom doesn't use cookies, so no consent banner is required for your analytics.

claims.text: The all-sites view includes totals like current visitors and bounce rate
claims.verbatim: including totals for things like current visitors and bounce rate.

claims.text: UTM tracking shows ad campaign and newsletter link performance

claims.text: Custom events can measure signups, downloads and purchases
claims.verbatim: Measure the actions that matter to your business, from signups and downloads to purchases.

claims.text: Events can carry a monetary value beyond pageviews
claims.verbatim: and attach a monetary value to see more than pageviews.

claims.text: Email reports can go to anyone for one or several sites without login
claims.verbatim: for one site or several, so anyone can keep track of your analytics without logging in.

claims.text: Fathom advertises unlimited data retention
claims.verbatim: Unlimited data retention

claims.text: History is kept for as long as you remain a customer

claims.text: Data can be viewed from signup until now, even if that is 30 years
claims.verbatim: from the day you started using Fathom until right now, even if that's 30 years of data.

claims.text: The script is pitched as not weighing down the website

claims.text: The lightweight script keeps pages fast while showing what's working

claims.text: Installation is a single script tag in the page head

proposal.pricing: Pageview-tiered plans shared across all sites on the account: $15/month for up to 100,000 monthly pageviews (50 sites included) rising through $25/$45/$60/$100/$140/$200/$290/$380/$470 per month up to 25,000,000 monthly pageviews, with 'Custom' pricing for 'Over 25,000,000 monthly pageviews'; extra site packs cost $10/month (or $100/year) per 50 sites, up to 15 packs; custom events count toward the pageview allowance; every plan starts with a 7-day free trial.
proposal.free_entry: 7-day free trial requiring a card ('Your card is not charged until the trial ends, and we'll email you before your plan starts billing'); no indefinite free tier; a no-signup live demo dashboard is also offered ('View a live demo').
proposal.icp: Positioned for buyers who want a privacy-focused Google Analytics alternative; described on-page as used by 'Fortune 100s, pioneers of the Open Web, Premier League football clubs, banks, and governments around the world,' with dedicated sections for European companies and agencies.
proposal.why: Fathom pitches a single dashboard where 'Sites on a plan share your monthly pageviews' and every plan 'includes at least 50 sites' (usefathom.com, usefathom.com/pricing), and like Plausible it is cookieless with 'No cookie banners required' — Plausible's own docs state 'No cookies, no personal data collection, no consent banners required' (E203). That supports comparing the two on a multi-site, cookieless footing. But Fathom's own pricing page lists the same usage-tiered structure as Plausible's — $15/month up to 100,000 monthly pageviews rising to $470/month at 25,000,000, with a Custom tier above that — just as Plausible's Starter plan is itself priced per pageview tier (E328). Neither company's own pages show a flat fee, so the discovery hypothesis's 'flat-fee' framing for Fathom is not supported by what either site actually publishes.
